title: Everyone Saw
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Heiji, Kazuha, Ran, Kogoro Mouri, Inspector Megure, Inspector Otaki, Detective Takagi) omitted by convention. Two deaths appear in this two-part episode: Fuura's shooting in the elevator is the case's actual murder (culprit: Naoko Izutsu); Mizuki's hanging is a genuine suicide that Mizuki himself staged to look like an impossible murder in order to posthumously frame Fuura for driving him to it -- his plan failed only because the stakeout police closed it as suicide before the murder theory could take hold, and Otaki/Heiji's re-investigation in part 1 exists purely to unravel that staging, not to solve a second murder. It is included here as backstory because it supplies Izutsu's real motive (Mizuki was her old teacher) and because Mizuki's own frame-up trick (decoy chair vs. real overturned bin) directly parallels Izutsu's later trick and is solved the same way -- by comparing two physical facts against each other. Correction vs. the old lower-fidelity case file: it placed all three suspects (Mutsu, Yoda, Izutsu) 'at' the elevator at the moment of the apparent live suicide (was_at l1/e2); the transcript does not support this -- only Nanami-san (a witness, not a suspect) and the detective party were at the elevator then. Mutsu, Yoda and Izutsu are the three residents-without-alibis interviewed afterward in their own flats. The old file also gave Izutsu's motive as 'unspecified'; the transcript states it explicitly (revenge for, and completion of, her mentor Mizuki's plan against Fuura). case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The GOODBYE spray message reads as a suicide note, but its placement splits the window exactly where the two video panels join, masking the seam between the tablets.

The camera was sprayed with a right hand, the gun was fired left-handed to match Fuura, and Izutsu -- seen using her right hand for a towel, book and lighter -- offered her left hand for the gunpowder residue check.
The chair by the body was too short to explain the hanging, but a nearby overturned bin, with spilled pencil shavings, was exactly tall enough -- exposing the chair as a planted decoy.

edges.detail: staged his own death to look like an impossible murder so investigators would eventually suspect Fuura
invited him to a nearby shop under the pretext of a new stock client
swapped Fuura's own watch for Mizuki's, to make the stopped time match her pre-recorded footage
